subject: Social Habits
title: Welcome to school
objectives: Children will say or show their name and recognise their teacher.
Children will separate from a parent with support and return happily.
content: Learning names, meeting the teacher and the classroom, and practising saying goodbye and hello again.
teachingActivities: Greet every child by name at the door; keep the first days calm and predictable; allow a parent to stay briefly if needed; never rush a crying child; give a comfort object a safe place; sing the same songs every day.
learnerActivities: Respond to their name, recognise the teacher and settle in the classroom with adult support.
assessment: Observe whether each child responds to their name, settles with support and says or waves goodbye.
expectedOutcomes: Settles in the classroom with adult support.

lessons.title: My name
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will hear and respond to their own name.
successCriteria: Looks up when their name is called
Says or shows their name with support
lessons.previousKnowledge: This is the first week of school. Children arrive with different home experiences and some may be upset to leave their parents.
lessons.starter: Sit in a circle and sing "Hello, hello, what is your name?" while looking at each child with a smile.
teacherActivities: Hold up each name card and say the child’s name warmly.
Roll a soft ball to each child and say their name.
Say the names of friends in the circle together.
Sing the name song again, using every name.
learnerActivities: Child looks and smiles or says their name.
Child catches or touches the ball.
Children look at friends and wave.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Hold up each name card and say the child’s name warmly. Children: Child looks and smiles or says their name.
Step 2. Teacher: Roll a soft ball to each child and say their name. Children: Child catches or touches the ball.
Step 3. Teacher: Say the names of friends in the circle together. Children: Children look at friends and wave.
Step 4. Teacher: Sing the name song again, using every name. Children: Children clap and sing along.

practical.title: Name circle
steps: Roll the ball to each child and say their name.
practical.safety: Use a very soft ball and sit children away from walls and furniture. Never push a child to speak; accept a smile or a point.

differentiation.support: Sit close to the child and use their photograph and name together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to roll the ball and say a friend’s name.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What is your name?
questions.expected: The child says or points to their name.

expectedOutcomes: Joins the name song with a smile or action
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye to each name and say "See you tomorrow."
lessons.homeConnection: Say your child’s name warmly and let them say or show it to family members.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "hear and respond to their own name" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Hello, hello, what is your name? Hello, hello, I am glad you came.

lessons.title: My teacher and my classroom
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will recognise their teacher and the main areas of the classroom.
successCriteria: Points to the teacher when asked
Visits the book corner and toy area with support
lessons.previousKnowledge: This is the first week of school. Children arrive with different home experiences and some may be upset to leave their parents.
resources: Labels for the book corner, toy area and toilet
lessons.starter: Use the puppet to say "Good morning! I am your teacher’s friend. Let us look at our classroom."
teacherActivities: Introduce yourself by name and show a photo of the teacher.
Walk around the room and name each area: books, toys, toilet and mat.
Show the picture timetable and say what happens next.
Let each child choose an area to visit with you.
learnerActivities: Children look and point to the teacher.
Child chooses and plays for a short time.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Introduce yourself by name and show a photo of the teacher. Children: Children look and point to the teacher.
Step 2. Teacher: Walk around the room and name each area: books, toys, toilet and mat. Children: Children walk with the teacher.
Step 3. Teacher: Show the picture timetable and say what happens next. Children: Children look at the pictures.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child choose an area to visit with you. Children: Child chooses and plays for a short time.

practical.title: Classroom walk
steps: Let each child choose a place to play.
practical.safety: Check the room for hazards before children arrive and stay close to children who wander. Keep doors closed and the gate secure.

differentiation.support: Hold the child’s hand and walk to one area at a time.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to show a friend one place in the classroom.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Finds at least one area of the classroom
lessons.conclusion: Sing the goodbye song and wave to the classroom.
lessons.homeConnection: Talk about school with your child in a happy voice and say you will always come back.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "recognise their teacher and the main areas of the classroom" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Saying goodbye and hello again
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will practise a short goodbye and a happy hello again.
lessons.previousKnowledge: This is the first week of school. Children arrive with different home experiences and some may be upset to leave their parents.
resources: A toy door or a screen
lessons.starter: Show the puppet who goes behind the screen and says "Goodbye!" then pops back with "Hello again!"
teacherActivities: Play the puppet goodbye and hello game.
Let each child hide a soft toy and bring it back.
Say "Mummy always comes back" in a calm, happy voice.
Practise a short goodbye wave at the door with a friend.
learnerActivities: Child hides the toy and finds it.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Play the puppet goodbye and hello game. Children: Children wave and say hello.
Step 2. Teacher: Let each child hide a soft toy and bring it back. Children: Child hides the toy and finds it.
Step 3. Teacher: Say "Mummy always comes back" in a calm, happy voice. Children: Children listen and wave.
Step 4. Teacher: Practise a short goodbye wave at the door with a friend. Children: Child waves and says bye.

practical.title: Goodbye and hello
steps: Bring it back and say hello again.
practical.safety: Stay close to a child who is upset and never leave a distressed child alone. Keep the play calm and gentle.

differentiation.support: Wave together and let the child hold a comfort toy.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to say goodbye to a friend and hello again.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What do we say when we go?
What do we say when we come back?

expectedOutcomes: Smiles when a toy or adult returns
lessons.conclusion: Sing the goodbye song and wave together.
lessons.homeConnection: Say a short, loving goodbye every day and promise to return.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "practise a short goodbye and a happy hello again" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Playing with new friends
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will play beside other children and notice their names.
successCriteria: Looks at a friend and smiles
lessons.previousKnowledge: This is the first week of school. Children arrive with different home experiences and some may be upset to leave their parents.
resources: Matching toys such as blocks and cars
lessons.starter: Put out two of each toy and say "Let us find a friend with the same toy."
teacherActivities: Show two matching toys and pair children beside each other.
Say each friend’s name as they play.
Show how to offer a toy with a smile.
Wave to the friend and say bye when finished.
learnerActivities: Child offers a toy to a friend.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show two matching toys and pair children beside each other. Children: Children sit beside a friend.
Step 2. Teacher: Say each friend’s name as they play. Children: Child looks at the friend.
Step 3. Teacher: Show how to offer a toy with a smile. Children: Child offers a toy to a friend.
Step 4. Teacher: Wave to the friend and say bye when finished. Children: Child waves and says bye.

practical.title: Play beside a friend
practical.safety: Use large toys with no small parts that can be swallowed and supervise closely. Step in gently if a child grabs.

differentiation.support: Sit with the child and play beside one friend.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to name a friend they played with.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Who is your friend?
questions.expected: Says or points to a friend.

expectedOutcomes: Says or points to a friend
lessons.conclusion: Tidy the toys together and wave goodbye.
lessons.homeConnection: Arrange short play dates or play beside siblings and name the other child.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "play beside other children and notice their names" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 1 settling check
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child is settling at school.
successCriteria: Settles in the classroom with support
lessons.previousKnowledge: This is the first week of school. Children arrive with different home experiences and some may be upset to leave their parents.
lessons.starter: Sing the welcome song and invite children to play at three familiar areas.
teacherActivities: Set up three areas: name circle, play and book corner.
Observe each child’s response to name, mood and play and note it.
Record each child’s level and a note for parents.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three areas: name circle, play and book corner. Children: Children move between areas freely.
Step 2. Teacher: Observe each child’s response to name, mood and play and note it. Children: Children play and explore.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and a note for parents. Children: Children join the goodbye song.

practical.title: Settling observation
practical.safety: Keep an adult at every area and watch for distressed children. Keep the environment calm and safe.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult close by and a comfort object.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to welcome a new friend.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: responds to name; separates from a parent with support; recognises the teacher; plays near others.

questions.question: What is your name?
questions.expected: The child says or shows it.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 1
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye and say "See you tomorrow."
lessons.homeConnection: Share a short note about how your child settled and how to keep goodbyes short.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child is settling at school" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
